scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by telling my mom she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my mom has some issues with not taking her kids to the doctor, even when they're sick. I remember when I was a kid, she didn't take me to the doctor, and I ended up in the hospital for weeks. That was really scary and almost cost me my life. I told her that's not okay, and she kind of brushed it off. That made me upset because I feel like she's putting her kids at risk again. Then, another time, she asked me to get her a drink and said, "You should know what I like, I've raised you for 26 years!" I responded that I don't know because my grandparents actually raised me, so I don't know much about her. She got upset and cried, saying I was trying to make her seem bad. I tried to explain I wasn't being mean, just pointing out her actions were not cool. Later, I had to talk to her about my brother's phone. She was taking his phone, which I paid for, and using it. I told her I don't want to take it back because I don't want my brother to be punished, but if she keeps doing it, I will. She got upset, started yelling and crying, and said I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly that she kind of is. She had a meltdown, said she doesn't need me in her life, and left. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't great to me. I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. I think about why I said what I did. I was hurt and scared because of her past actions, especially with the doctor thing. I felt like she wasn't taking responsibility for her kids' health. When she asked me about the drink, it felt like she was trying to make me feel guilty for not knowing her better, but I didn't grow up with her, so it's not my fault. With the phone, I was trying to protect my brother from being punished for her actions. I felt like she was taking advantage of him, and I had to set boundaries. When she accused me of making her look bad, I couldn't hold back my feelings because I've been hurt by her for so long. But now, my family is upset with me. They think I shouldn't have been so harsh, even if she wasn't perfect. Maybe they think I should have handled it more gently or not confronted her at all. I'm confused because I feel like I was standing up for myself and my brother, but they see it differently. I wonder if there's a better way to handle this without causing such a big argument. Maybe I could have talked to her more calmly or found a different approach. But at the same time, I feel like her actions were wrong, and I had to say something. I also think about the impact on my relationship with her. She left after the argument, and now I'm worried about losing her. But I also don't want to stay in a relationship where she keeps making these mistakes without taking responsibility. In the end, I'm not sure if what I did was right or wrong. I was trying to protect myself and my brother, but it caused a lot of hurt and tension. Maybe there's a middle ground where I can express my feelings without being so confrontational. But I also don't want to ignore the issues because they're important to me.
